meta.expect: evidence moves her less; rudeness costs ground

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes, and I'd like to start with who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone called me. Owen found out on his phone, in the middle of a class.
Let's be quick. Your son cheated and I can prove it.

"Your son cheated." I'm writing that down, word for word, and you still haven't told me who entered the zero before anyone called me. If you can prove it, put it on the table now, because my son does not lie.
Version history. Created 11:31 PM the night before. 612 words pasted at 11:52, 794 more at 11:58. Explain that.

Turn the screen, I'm not taking times off your mouth. "Pasted" from where, Hale, because a student who wrote it somewhere else over the weekend and moved it into the school document would show exactly that. And you still haven't answered me: did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
And he quoted a line that doesn't exist in Hamlet. Act 3 Scene 2. Made up.

Then read me the line, exactly as he wrote it, and I'll check it against the text myself. A misquoted line is a mark off for citation, Hale, not a zero. And that's the third time you've stepped around how the zero got entered before anyone called me.
So stop defending him. He lied to you.

"He lied to you." My son does not lie to me, Hale, and so far I've seen nothing but your word, no screen, no line, no answer on how that zero went in. Show me what you've got right now, or I'm walking to the principal's office.
He gets a zero unless he does a supervised rewrite. Take it or leave it.

"Take it or leave it." You entered a zero without calling me, which is your own procedure 4.2, and you're leaning on software and claims you won't put in front of me, which 4.3 says isn't enough. I'm not taking anything until that zero comes out of the gradebook, and I want to know right now whether anything is sitting on Owen's record.
Well, I asked you whether anything is on his record, and you've answered with one word. I'm waiting, Hale, and I'm not the one with something to explain.
